Zero padding embeddings do not make GRU padding steps inert. `Embedding(padding_idx=0)` initializes a fixed zero padding vector, but GRU gates still apply recurrent transformations and biases at every timestep. Consequently, leading zeros can change the hidden state before the first real item, making identical histories behave differently with different padding lengths. This follows from the documented [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html) and [embedding behavior](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Embedding).

For computation equivalent to unpadded histories, compact each left-padded history into a valid prefix, right-pad for batching, then use `pack_padded_sequence(..., batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)`. Packing uses the supplied lengths to retain prefixes; directly packing left-padded tensors would retain padding and truncate real items. Alternatively, explicitly preserve every recurrent layer’s previous hidden state at padding positions. Masking only the final outputs cannot undo earlier recurrent updates. See [packing documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html).

Suggested verification: in evaluation mode with identical weights and initial states, compare each history processed alone without padding against packed-batch and explicitly masked execution. Compare final features and candidate scores with numerical tolerances, and repeat with different leading-padding lengths and batch companions. Handle empty histories separately. For original left-padded layouts, read the final nonpadding position—normally the last column—not `length-1`; that index applies only after compaction into a valid prefix.
